name: Berkson’s paradox: selection creates an association
conclusion: (Pr(Y | do(X)) = Pr(Y | do(~X))) & (Pr(Y | X & S) < Pr(Y | ~X & S))
description: Two independent causes become associated after selecting their common consequence S. This Boolean illustration selects cases where X or Y is true. Regular is off because selection is deterministic.

name: M-bias: a harmful pretreatment adjustment
graph: U -> X; U -> Z; V -> Z; V -> Y
conclusion: (Pr(Y | do(X)) = Pr(Y | do(~X))) & (Pr(Y | X) = Pr(Y | ~X)) & (Pr(Y | X & Z) < Pr(Y | ~X & Z))
description: X has no causal effect on Y and no marginal association with Y. Conditioning on the collider Z creates an apparent protective effect. U and V are explicitly represented independent Boolean background causes; every mechanism is positive.

source.title: Ding and Miratrix: M-bias and butterfly bias

name: Bias amplification: controlling an instrument
graph: Z -> X; U -> X; U -> Y; X -> Y
description: The true risk difference is 1/5. The observational difference is 8/25; standardizing over the instrument Z gives 31/80 and increases the bias. U is an explicit Boolean common cause whose influence is left unadjusted in those two comparisons.

evaluations.expression: (Pr(Y | X & Z) - Pr(Y | ~X & Z))*Pr(Z) + (Pr(Y | X & ~Z) - Pr(Y | ~X & ~Z))*Pr(~Z)

name: Treatment–confounder feedback
graph: A -> L; L -> B; L -> Y; B -> Y
conclusion: (Pr(Y | A & B) - Pr(Y | ~A & ~B) > Pr(Y | do(A, B)) - Pr(Y | do(~A, ~B))) & (Pr(Y | do(A, B)) - Pr(Y | do(~A, ~B)) > (Pr(Y | A & B & L) - Pr(Y | ~A & ~B & L))*Pr(L) + (Pr(Y | A & B & ~L) - Pr(Y | ~A & ~B & ~L))*Pr(~L))
description: A is early treatment, L a later covariate, and B later treatment. Every causal path from A to Y passes through L, which also confounds B’s effect. The joint treatment contrast is 1/2; its observational analogue is 17/25. Averaging over the population’s L distribution instead of its treatment-specific distribution gives 1/5.

source.title: Hernán and Robins: Causal Inference: What If

evaluations.expression: (Pr(Y | A & B & L) - Pr(Y | ~A & ~B & L))*Pr(L) + (Pr(Y | A & B & ~L) - Pr(Y | ~A & ~B & ~L))*Pr(~L)

name: Front-door adjustment
graph: U -> X; U -> Y; X -> M; M -> Y
description: U is an explicit Boolean common cause, and M mediates the entire effect of X on Y. The front-door expression uses only X, M and Y and recovers the intervention probability 11/20. This illustrates the formula in a specified Boolean model; it is not a general latent-variable identification procedure.

evaluations.expression: Pr(M | X)*(Pr(Y | M & X)*Pr(X) + Pr(Y | M & ~X)*Pr(~X)) + Pr(~M | X)*(Pr(Y | ~M & X)*Pr(X) + Pr(Y | ~M & ~X)*Pr(~X))

name: Positivity failure: an unseen treatment branch
description: Observation never reaches X=true. The premises therefore leave that mechanism branch undetermined, so the proposed intervention probability is not entailed. The returned countermodel gives one possible value, not an identified effect. Regular is off to allow zero observational support.

source.title: Hernán and Robins: Causal Inference: What If

name: Simpson’s paradox: E, M and A
graph: E -> M; E -> A; M -> A
description: The supplied E/M/A table has a positive overall M–A association (7/13 versus 6/13), but a negative association in each E group. The displayed DAG treats E as a common cause of M and A. Under that causal assumption, the intervention rates are 19/40 versus 21/40; the conclusion states the reversal. The counts alone do not determine the DAG.
dataNote: Probabilities reproduce the supplied E/M/A table.
